q: Can an EV charging station business earn carbon credits in India?
title: Carbon credits for EV charging stations
short: Possibly, through a voluntary methodology such as Verra's VM0038 for electric vehicle charging systems, which credits fuel displaced from petrol and diesel vehicles minus the grid electricity used. Whether you can depends on additionality, who owns the claim, and enough charging volume to cover validation and verification costs.
audience: Charge point operators and fleet electrification startups in India

sections.h: How the reduction is worked out
p: VM0038 compares the emissions of the fossil fuel vehicles that the electric vehicles replace with the emissions of the electricity delivered through the chargers. The baseline uses vehicle efficiency and fuel factors; the project side uses metered kWh and a grid factor set by the methodology. Metered energy data per charger is the base of the whole calculation.

ol: Ownership: the charge point operator, the fleet owner, the vehicle maker and the site host could each claim the same reduction. Settle in writing who holds the right before registering.
Additionality: the methodology sets its own test. A network that is profitable on charging fees alone, or required by a concession or tender, may fail it.
Double claiming: a fleet that reports the same switch in its own inventory or sells it as a separate claim reduces what you can credit.
Volume: credits per charger are modest, so grouped projects across many sites are the usual route.

sections.h: Programme status to check before you start
ul: Verra: confirm the current version of VM0038 and any rules on India.
ICVCM: check whether EV charging methodologies have been assessed for the Core Carbon Principles label; many buyers now ask for it.
India CCTS offset mechanism: check whether BEE's list of approved offset methodologies includes e-mobility before planning around it.

sections.h: How this differs from a factory project
p: A factory fuel switch cuts its own Scope 1. A charging business earns a reduction that happens in other people's vehicles, so the evidence must show the vehicles are real, would otherwise run on fossil fuel, and are not claimed twice. That makes contracts with fleet customers as important as meter data.

example.title: Worked estimate: ten chargers for car fleets
lines: Energy delivered: 300,000 kWh a year; project emissions 300,000 x 0.710 = 213,000 kg CO2
At 0.15 kWh per km, that is 300,000 / 0.15 = 2,000,000 km
Diesel car baseline at 15 km per litre: 2,000,000 / 15 = 133,333 litres x 2.68 = 357,333 kg CO2
Reduction: 357,333 to 213,000 = 144,333 kg, about 144 tonnes CO2 a year
example.note: Labelled estimate: vehicle efficiency and mileage are assumptions, 2.68 kg CO2 per litre is the IPCC 2006 diesel default and 0.710 is the CEA weighted average grid factor. The methodology may require a different grid factor, such as a combined margin.

senseible: Senseible shows carbon credit eligibility signals from activity records such as electricity bills and fuel invoices, and keeps that evidence traceable. It is not a registry and plays no part in validation or issuance.
